blog: The name tag was a prop for the poster.

Our Police Union asked me to pose for this photo to encourage officers to reach out for help. I was two years into the best job I ever had: the K9 Unit, one of 40 K9 handlers out of 6,000 officers. I felt like I was on top of the world. Nothing could hurt me.
Less than ten years later, this is exactly where I ended up.
I went a thousand miles an hour. Over a thousand violent incidents, including shootings, in an era when nobody in policing talked about mental health. You cleared the job and went to the next one.

I didn't see what it was doing to me. Scanning every room I walked into. Lying awake, unable to switch off. More cynical every year. Drinking to take the edge off. Pulling away from the people closest to me, and blaming the bosses and the politics for all of it.
I left at 32 with PTSD, depression, and years of suicidal thoughts behind me. No pension. No payout. No plan.
I was the face of a poster telling cops to ask for help. I never imagined it would one day be about me.
That's why this quiz exists. The questions you just answered are the warning signs I missed in myself, and the ones I now see in the officers I work with.

Since 2017, I've worked with police through The Strong Life Project, including hundreds of live workshops with thousands of law enforcement officers both in Australia and the USA. More than 1,400 officers have rated the training, and 91.8% gave it 5 out of 5.

I'm not a psychologist. I'm a cop who lived it, rebuilt, and has spent 20 years learning how. I have been through divorce, family court and dealt with many of the other challenges that a policing career creates and come out the other side.
